req.title: Delete only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to delete a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that only the author of a post should be able to delete it, and any other user should receive a 403 Forbidden response. This ensures proper authorization control over post deletions. The test suite includes a positive case where the author deletes their own post, a negative case where a non-author attempts to delete a post, and a boundary case where the post does not exist.

tests.name: Author deletes own post
preconditions: Post with id 1 exists and is authored by 'test'
actions: Send POST request to /1/delete as user 'test'
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

tests.name: Non-author attempts to delete post
preconditions: Post with id 1 exists and is authored by 'test'
actions: Send POST request to /1/delete as user 'other'
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 403

tests.name: Delete non-existent post
preconditions: Post with id 2 does not exist
actions: Send POST request to /2/delete as user 'test'
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
